answer: At a wharf, agents allocate crane slots for crystal cargo by token-weighted vote. A cipher hides ballot choices until the tally. Every token stays in escrow until voting closes and supplies one unit of weight; a shared ledger marks it as used for that vote. An attacker distributing S tokens among n aliases still controls only S weight. More influence requires buying or renting more capital and keeping it locked. The rule needs correct escrow and tallying, with no identity-based bonus; wealthy or colluding token holders can still dominate.
